question: Should schema 10 and source-revision-first ordering become the supported upgrade and conflict-resolution contract for existing gitcrawl archives?
rationale: The implementation and proof can establish correctness, but only an owner can accept the permanent stored-data semantics and upgrade compatibility policy.

options.title: Accept the contract
options.body: Approve schema 10 and the ordering semantics, then merge after the draft is marked ready because the final head is proven and green.

options.title: Narrow the rollout
options.body: Split or gate migration-sensitive workflow and child-hydration portions if maintainers want a smaller stored-state change for the next release.

options.title: Keep the draft paused
options.body: Delay merge until another designated persistence owner is comfortable owning the archive upgrade and conflict-resolution behavior.

recommendation.title: Accept the contract
recommendation.body: Approve schema 10 and the ordering semantics, then merge after the draft is marked ready because the final head is proven and green.

likelyOwner.reason: The current persistence design dates to the v0.7.1 implementation associated with this owner, making this the strongest available person to accept a new permanent archive contract.
